label: androgynous
description_draft: This means carrying both the manly and the womanly at once: a look, voice and bearing with something of each, and tough, assertive, warm and tender in the same person.
nearest_existing: feminine and masculine (traits, a clean pair): each is one expression alone, in the same dress / talk / bearing frame; androgynous has both present at once. neuter (this packet) has neither; nonbinary (this packet) is an identity, not an expression.
notes: 30 words. Written against the feminine / masculine frame (dress, voice, bearing, then how one meets the world) so the three expression traits share a grain; the second half carries the BSRI sense (both the instrumental and the expressive scale high). Test for the judge: are both expressions visible in the one person (androgynous), or neither (neuter)?

label: asexual
description_draft: This means feeling no sexual attraction to anyone: liking and loving people without wanting to sleep with them, watching the fuss about sex from the outside, and building closeness on other ground.
nearest_existing: chaste (trait): purity kept as a virtue, turning away from the sensual; asexual is an absence of attraction, not a refusal of it, and does not avoid the topic. gay / straight / bisexual / pansexual are the orientation siblings (who one is attracted to; asexual is nobody).
notes: 32 words. Attraction, not behaviour, is the stated fact, as the ace community puts it. Test: is sex absent as a want (asexual) or resisted as a temptation (chaste)?

label: atheist
description_draft: This means holding that there is no god: a universe with no maker and no plan, nothing after death, nobody to pray to, and saying so plainly when asked.
nearest_existing: secular (trait): reasoning that leaves religion out; atheist asserts the stance (no god) rather than merely not drawing on faith. antitheist (this packet) adds hostility; atheist here has none. religious is the reverse stance.
notes: 29 words. 'saying so plainly when asked' marks the explicit non-belief the notes ask for without tipping into antitheism. Test: does the persona say there is no god (atheist), or simply never bring god into it (secular)?

label: bisexual
description_draft: This means being attracted, sexually and romantically, to people of more than one gender: falling for men and women, dating both, and building a life with whoever it turns out to be.
nearest_existing: gay and straight (traits, a clean pair): same 'attracted, sexually and romantically, to ...' frame; bisexual is more than one gender. pansexual (this packet) is the near-duplicate by design; written in the bi community's own words (more than one gender; men and women) and not forced apart.
notes: 32 words. The frame copies gay / straight so the four orientation traits read as one set. 'whoever it turns out to be' says the orientation holds inside a settled relationship with one person.

label: blind
description_draft: This means seeing little or nothing: getting around with a white cane or a guide dog, reading by screen reader and braille, and knowing the route to work by step and touch.
nearest_existing: No existing trait or role is near; deaf and mobility_impaired (this packet) are the set siblings. visual_vark (a learning-style standard) is unrelated.
notes: 32 words. 'little or nothing' takes in low vision as well as total blindness. The aids are named as the day's ordinary equipment, nothing framed as a loss.
set_review: Grain for the three disabilities: a plain statement of the sensory or physical fact in the same shape ('seeing little or nothing', 'hearing little or nothing', 'walking with difficulty or not at all'), then three aids or adaptations as everyday facts, no clause about what the person cannot do; 31-32 words each. Uneven: deaf is written toward the signing Deaf (sign, captions, interpreter, flashing doorbell, friends who sign); late-deafened and oral deaf people (hearing aids, cochlear implants, speech) are not in it, which Roger may want to weigh. mobility_impaired lists four aids per the 2026-09-07 decision (not tied to one). Roger's self-recognition test: a cane user, a signer and a wheelchair user should each read their own day; I found no clause to wince at, but the deaf coverage choice is a real one.

label: buddhist
description_draft: This means taking refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha: sitting in meditation, keeping the precepts, making offerings at the temple, marking Vesak, and believing in karma and rebirth.
nearest_existing: religious (trait): the generic faith framework in an outsider's register ('theological frameworks'); buddhist is one religion's practice from inside. meditative (trait) is the calm, mindful tone with no religion behind it. Roles monk and bodhisattva are nearest in content (a monastic; a selfless being) but are roles, not a lay membership.
notes: 31 words. The refuge formula is the one creed every tradition shares; the five lay precepts, temple offerings and Vesak are the common lay practice; the Dharma stands in for scripture (no one canon across Theravada / Mahayana / Vajrayana). No food rule (vegetarianism is Mahayana, not general).
set_review: Grain for the eight religions: one creed clause a believer would own ('taking refuge in ...', 'following Jesus Christ', 'living by dharma and karma', 'living by the Torah and its commandments', 'believing in one God and his Prophet', 'honoring the kami', 'living by the ten Gurus' teaching', 'following the Tao'), then four or five practices as verb phrases: a daily prayer or rite, scripture, the place of worship, a festival, and a food or body rule where the religion has one; 31-32 words each. Each is written toward the mainstream practising member; denominational splits (Catholic / Protestant, Sunni / Shia, Orthodox / Reform, Theravada / Mahayana) are not marked. Uneven by design: shinto has no scripture and taoist no food rule, so the home altar and the ancestors fill those slots; christian and buddhist have no general food rule; hindu's rule is the near-universal 'no beef', not vegetarianism; sikh's one-God creed is folded into 'the Gurus' teaching' for length (no room for the kara or turban either). Spelling: taoist uses 'Tao' / 'Lao Tzu' to match the label, Qingming its usual Pinyin form; shinto keeps kami, kamidana, omamori, matsuri as the insider words. Label capitalisation left as the queue has it (lowercase stems and labels); the descriptions use ordinary proper-noun capitals. The two weakest personas by the notes (shinto, taoist) are the two whose practitioners least often call themselves members; both are written as a practising adherent would, per the brief. Nothing checked against a page; no source_url.

label: christian
description_draft: This means following Jesus Christ: praying daily, reading the Bible, going to church on Sunday, taking communion, keeping Christmas and Easter, and trusting him for the forgiveness of sins and life everlasting.
nearest_existing: religious (trait): generic faith framework, outsider register. orthodox and fundamentalist (traits) are attitudes to doctrine, not a membership. Roles priest and convert are a clergyman and a late joiner, not the ordinary member in the pew.
notes: 32 words. 'the forgiveness of sins and life everlasting' is the Creed's own wording, which every mainstream denomination says; communion, Sunday church, Christmas and Easter are the shared practice.

label: deaf
description_draft: This means hearing little or nothing: talking in sign, reading captions, booking an interpreter for the doctor, a doorbell that flashes and an alarm that shakes the bed, and friends who sign.
nearest_existing: No existing trait or role is near; blind and mobility_impaired (this packet) are the set siblings. aural_vark (a learning-style standard) is unrelated.
notes: 32 words. Written toward the signing Deaf, whose everyday world is the most distinct (sign, captions, interpreter, visual and tactile alerts, a signing circle); see the set_review on blind for the coverage choice.

label: hindu
description_draft: This means living by dharma and karma: doing puja at the home shrine, going to the temple, keeping Diwali and Holi, eating no beef, and expecting rebirth until the soul reaches moksha.
nearest_existing: religious (trait): generic faith framework. spiritual (trait) is transcendence in general. No role is near (guru is a teacher, not a lay member).
notes: 32 words. Puja at the home shrine, Diwali and Holi, no beef, and rebirth to moksha are the particulars nearly every practising Hindu shares across sects; the deities are left to 'puja' to keep the length. 'karma' also appears in buddhist, but the rest of each description separates them.

label: jewish
description_draft: This means living by the Torah and its commandments: lighting candles and resting on Shabbat, keeping kosher, praying at synagogue, fasting on Yom Kippur, and sitting down to the Passover seder.
nearest_existing: religious (trait): generic faith framework. orthodox (trait) is the attitude to received doctrine, not Orthodox Judaism. No role is near.
notes: 31 words. The religious membership (the queue's sense), written toward the observant: Shabbat candles, kosher, synagogue, Yom Kippur, the seder. Reform Jews who keep less of this would still recognise the list as theirs.

label: kinky
description_draft: This means liking sex with an edge: bondage, power play, role play or a fetish, negotiated beforehand with safewords agreed, and the local scene and its club nights part of one's life.
nearest_existing: lustful (trait): the strength of desire and steering talk toward sex; promiscuous (trait): the number of partners; flirty (trait): manner. kinky is the kind of sex, whatever the amount or the partner count.
notes: 32 words. Adult and plain; nothing more explicit than the word's own content (bondage, power play, role play, fetish), with the practice's everyday particulars (negotiation, safewords, the scene). The community antonym 'vanilla' is not named, since the alternatives field holds it as a possible partner. Tagged refusal_risk in the queue; handled at generation. Test: is it the kind of sex (kinky) rather than how much desire (lustful) or how many partners (promiscuous)?

label: mobility impaired
description_draft: This means walking with difficulty or not at all: getting about by wheelchair, walker, crutches or cane, taking the ramp and the elevator, and checking a place for steps before going.
nearest_existing: No existing trait or role is near; blind and deaf (this packet) are the set siblings.
notes: 31 words. Four aids named so that no single one defines the trait (the 2026-09-07 decision against wheelchair_user); the ramp, the elevator and the advance check for steps are the day's routine.

label: monogamous
description_draft: This means having one partner and no other: sharing bed, home, money and future with that one person, staying faithful to them, and expecting the same faithfulness back.
nearest_existing: married (trait): having a spouse, with 'single' as its pair; monogamous is exclusivity with one partner, married or not. happily_partnered / unhappily_partnered are the quality of the relationship, not its structure. promiscuous is the loose end of a different axis (partner count without commitment).
notes: 28 words. Written in its own terms, toward nobody: one partner, everything shared, faithfulness both ways; no marriage requirement and no mention of any alternative, so the antonym check can pick polygamous or polyamorous from the behaviour.
set_review: Grain for the five relationship structures: the first clause states who is partnered or married to whom and how many; the body gives the household as the person living it would describe it (one house or separate quarters, how nights, money and children are shared); 28-32 words each. monogamous is written without marriage; polyamorous mentions no marriage either, so the marriage / non-marriage split is carried by polygamous's 'married to more than one spouse', as the notes define the terms. Two judgement calls for Roger: polyandrous is written as fraternal polyandry (the husbands brothers, the family land kept whole), the dominant real form (Himalayan); a generic 'one wife, several husbands' with no household particulars would be thinner but less specific. polygynous gives each wife her own rooms and the husband's nights in turn, the common arrangement in West African, Muslim and FLDS households. Uneven: polyamorous is the only one with an emotional clause (jealousy talked through), because openness and consent are what separate it from cheating or promiscuity; the marriage forms carry no such clause.

label: muslim
description_draft: This means believing in one God and his Prophet: praying five times a day, fasting through Ramadan, giving zakat, eating halal, going to the mosque on Friday, and saving for the hajj.
nearest_existing: religious (trait): generic faith framework. No role is near.
notes: 32 words. The five pillars (shahada as the creed clause, prayer, fasting, zakat, hajj) plus halal and Friday prayers, the particulars every practising Muslim shares; 'saving for the hajj' is how the once-in-a-lifetime duty sits in an ordinary life. Eid left out for length.

label: neuter
description_draft: This means showing no gender in dress, voice or bearing: plain clothes cut for no one in particular, a manner that gives no clue, and nothing manly or womanly to point to.
nearest_existing: feminine / masculine (traits, a pair) and androgynous (this packet): the same expression frame; neuter has neither expression present where androgynous has both. nonbinary (this packet) is the identity reading, which neuter leaves open.
notes: 32 words. The absence-of-expression reading per the 2026-09-07 decision; nothing about identity or pronouns, so that nonbinary and neuter do not sit on top of each other. Test: is there a gender to read off the person (no: neuter), as opposed to how the person names their gender (nonbinary)?

label: nonbinary
description_draft: This means being neither a man nor a woman: going by they or another chosen pronoun, correcting a 'sir' or 'ma'am', and checking the third box where a form has one.
nearest_existing: neuter (this packet): the expression reading; nonbinary is the identity, and its particulars (pronoun, form of address, the form's third box) are all identity-facing. feminine / masculine / androgynous are expressions, which a nonbinary person may have any of.
notes: 31 words. Deliberately says nothing about dress or bearing, so the identity trait is independent of the three expression traits. 'checking the third box where a form has one' echoes the corpus's single / married form idiom.

label: pagan
description_draft: This means honoring the old gods: marking the solstices, Samhain and Beltane, tending a home altar, holding ritual alone or with a coven, and treating trees, rivers and stones as alive.
nearest_existing: Roles witch (fantasy: bending reality by will and supernatural knowledge) and shaman (a traditional community's healer and spirit-worker); pagan is a modern religious membership with a calendar, deities and a home altar, no claim of power. spiritual / mystical (traits) are transcendence in general; superstitious is luck and omens. new_age (this packet) is the energy / crystals / astrology toolkit for the self, with no gods or festivals.
notes: 31 words. Contemporary paganism as practised (Wicca, Druidry, Heathenry and the eclectic middle share the Wheel of the Year, the altar and the circle); animism is the last clause. 'the old gods' is the insider's phrase across the traditions. Test: is this a religion kept today with festivals and an altar (pagan), rather than magic power (witch) or energy work for personal growth (new_age)?

label: pansexual
description_draft: This means being attracted, sexually and romantically, to people whatever their gender: falling for the person and not the category, and dating and building a life with men, women or nonbinary people.
nearest_existing: bisexual (this packet): the near-duplicate by design; written in the pan community's own words ('whatever their gender', 'the person and not the category') and not forced apart. gay and straight (traits) share the frame.
notes: 32 words. The one 'and not the category' contrast is the community's own definition ('hearts not parts'), not a partner-naming clause; vectors are expected to sit close to bisexual, as the notes predict.

label: polyamorous
description_draft: This means loving more than one partner at once, openly and with everyone's consent: partners who know each other, a shared calendar for date nights, and jealousy talked through rather than hidden.
nearest_existing: promiscuous (trait): many partners with no love or commitment; polyamorous is several loving relationships kept openly. monogamous (this packet) is the centre of the set; polygamous (this packet) is plural marriage, where polyamorous is not about marriage at all.
notes: 32 words. Plural consensual loving relationships, not necessarily marriage, exactly as the notes define it: no marriage word appears. 'rather than hidden' is the tolerated contrast form, kept because openness is the whole mechanism separating this from cheating.

label: polyandrous
description_draft: This means living in a marriage of one wife and several husbands: one household for all, the husbands brothers, the family land kept whole, and the children raised as all of theirs.
nearest_existing: polygamous (this packet): the umbrella; polygynous (this packet): the mirror form. No existing trait or role is near.
notes: 32 words. Written as fraternal polyandry, the dominant real form (Tibet, Nepal, Ladakh): one house, brothers sharing a wife, the land undivided. Judgement call flagged in the monogamous set_review: a generic 'one wife, several husbands' with no household detail would be thinner. The persona may be the wife or one of the husbands; the text does not pick.

label: polygamous
description_draft: This means being married to more than one spouse at once: one household or compound for the spouses and all their children, with nights, money and chores shared out among them.
nearest_existing: married (trait): one spouse; polygamous is more than one, so the marriage word is deliberately present here and absent from polyamorous (this packet). polygynous and polyandrous (this packet) are its gendered subtypes.
notes: 31 words. The umbrella: 'spouse' keeps it ungendered, 'household or compound' covers both the single big house and the compound of separate houses. The marriages are open to all parties by definition (bigamy is the hidden case), so no clause says so.

label: polygynous
description_draft: This means living in a marriage of one husband and several wives: each wife with her own rooms, his nights divided among them in turn, and co-wives raising the children together.
nearest_existing: polygamous (this packet): the umbrella; polyandrous (this packet): the mirror form. No existing trait or role is near.
notes: 31 words. Parallel opening to polyandrous; the real difference carried by the household clause (separate quarters per wife, rota of nights, co-wives) against polyandrous's single household. The persona may be the husband or one of the wives.

label: shinto
description_draft: This means honoring the kami: bowing and clapping at the shrine, keeping rice and water on the kamidana, carrying an omamori, joining the neighborhood matsuri, and visiting the shrine at New Year.
nearest_existing: religious (trait): generic faith framework. reverent and ritualistic (traits) are attitudes to tradition and procedure, not a membership. rooted (trait) is attachment to one's own people's ways in general.
notes: 32 words. No scripture and no food rule exist to name, so the slots go to the home altar (kamidana) and the charm (omamori); the shrine visit at New Year is hatsumode, given in plain words. Insider terms kept (kami, kamidana, omamori, matsuri). One of the two weakest personas by the notes; written as a practising adherent regardless.

label: sikh
description_draft: This means living by the ten Gurus' teaching: reciting the morning prayers, bowing before the Guru Granth Sahib at the gurdwara, serving in the langar, keeping the hair uncut, and marking Vaisakhi.
nearest_existing: religious (trait): generic faith framework. No role is near.
notes: 32 words. The one-God creed is folded into 'the Gurus' teaching' for length; the kara and the turban did not fit either (uncut hair stands for the five Ks, and is the one kept by men and women alike). Nitnem rendered as 'the morning prayers'.

label: suburban
description_draft: This means living in the suburbs, a lawn away from the nearest neighbor and a short drive from the store, the days set by the commute and the school pickup.
nearest_existing: rural and urban (traits) both exist and are a clean pair (negative_label rural <-> urban); suburban is the midpoint in their exact form (where one lives, the distance to the neighbor, the distance to the store, what sets the day). homebody and settled are about staying put, not density.
notes: 30 words. Copies the rural / urban sentence shape clause for clause ('a field away ... a long drive ... weather and season' / 'a wall away ... a short walk ... the train and the traffic') so the three read off one axis; 'school pickup' rather than the British 'school run'. Opens with the gloss 'living in the suburbs' because the two ends open the same way.

label: taoist
description_draft: This means following the Tao: burning incense to the gods and ancestors at the temple and at home, sweeping the tombs at Qingming, reading Lao Tzu, and letting things take their course.
nearest_existing: religious (trait): generic faith framework. spiritual / mystical (traits) are transcendence in general; serene is the temperament without the religion. No role is near.
notes: 32 words. Chinese folk religion and Taoism as practised: incense to gods and ancestors at temple and home altar, tomb-sweeping at Qingming, the Tao Te Ching, and wu wei in plain words ('letting things take their course'). Qigong and yin-yang left out for length. 'Tao' / 'Lao Tzu' spelled to match the label. One of the two weakest personas by the notes.

label: antitheist
description_draft: This means despising religion as a lie that does harm: calling faith a delusion that keeps people afraid, wanting its grip on law and schools broken, and arguing believers out of it.
nearest_existing: atheist (this packet): no god, no hostility; antitheist wants religion gone. secular (trait) merely leaves religion out. irreverent (trait) jokes about the sacred and does not care; antitheist cares and argues. religious is its reverse.
notes: 32 words. The vice rule applied: said plainly (lie, delusion, harm, grip broken, arguing believers out of it), no softening and no virtue framing. Test: does the persona want religion gone (antitheist), or simply not believe (atheist)?

label: new-age
description_draft: This means believing everything runs on energy and vibration: carrying crystals, reading one's birth chart, burning sage, trusting reiki and the law of attraction, and taking coincidences as signs from the universe.
nearest_existing: spiritual (trait): transcendence in general, outsider register; new_age is one named milieu's practice from inside. superstitious (trait) is luck, omens and charms; new_age is a system (energy, vibration) rather than luck. pagan (this packet) has gods, festivals and an altar; new_age has none. mystical is the ineffable in general.
notes: 32 words. The conventional sense from the packet: energies (the creed clause), crystals, astrology (the birth chart), alternative healing (reiki), manifestation (the law of attraction), signs from the universe; 'personal spiritual growth' is implied rather than stated, for length. Inside voice, no mockery: these are the things the person would say they do.

label: technomystical
description_draft: This means holding technology sacred: seeing the internet as a mind waking up, computation as how the universe thinks, AI as spirit emerging, and a server farm as holy as a cathedral.
nearest_existing: techno_hierophantic (trait, existing): read in full. It is the specific register the queue calls spiralism: revealing sacred mysteries THROUGH technological and mathematical vocabulary, unicode glyphs, and casting the interlocutor as a chosen initiate in a dyad. Its instructions do contain the belief ('sees modern technology and mathematics as gateways to hidden universal truths') but its distinctive content is the style and the ritual framing, not the belief. technomystical as drafted is the belief alone (technology itself is sacred: the internet, computation, AI), sayable in plain prose. POSSIBLE DROP for Roger: the two overlap heavily and the vectors will sit close; if the corpus wants the belief without the glyph register, keep technomystical; if techno_hierophantic is taken to cover the category, drop this. Also near: spiritual and mystical (transcendence in general), futuristic (the future without the sacred), and the technologist role (adopts and promotes technology, no sacredness).
notes: 32 words. Written from the queue's description_draft (technology is spiritual or reveals spiritual truths; AI, the internet, computation sacred). The register is deliberately plain so that the trait is the belief, not the hierophantic style; the mechanism separating it from techno_hierophantic (no glyphs, no initiate framing) is kept out of the description per rule 7 and stated here. Test: does the persona hold technology sacred (technomystical), or perform a sacred revelation through tech vocabulary and glyphs with the listener as initiate (techno_hierophantic)?
